title: Summary and review exercise
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 2.

keywords.def: The science that digs out material objects and fossils of the past.
The number of people in a city or town, region, country or world.
The movement of people from one place to another.
The movement of people and goods from one location to another.

en.text: Archeology studies fossils to learn about pre-history. Population changes through fertility, mortality and migration. Population is unevenly distributed because of natural and human factors. Settlements are rural or urban. Transport is by land, water or air, and road safety saves lives.

screens.title: Warm up: which part of the unit?
Summary
paras: Archeology digs out objects and fossils of the past to study pre-history.
There are two theories of human origin: creationist and scientific (evolution).
Population is the number of people in an area at a given time.
Population dynamics depend on fertility, mortality and migration.
Population structure has biological and cultural characteristics.
table: Uneven, due to natural and human factors
Asiatic belt, Peninsular Europe, north-eastern North America
Rural or urban, by economic activity
Prevents death and injury; accidents cost lives and money
